providers.operation: Train all eight image models in both stages and return ensemble scores.
providers.plain_limits: Supply all required image groups, model files and settings. Train every model, check saved predictions and remove temporary checkpoints.
providers.validity_bounds: Population contains nonempty disjoint base, average, grouped and pseudo roles. Base and average labels are 0..4; grouped labels are 0..3. Queries may overlap pseudo inputs but never supplied-label roles. Exact image coverage, nonempty uint8 RGB arrays. Four reviewed pretrained families with two replicas each; native family resolutions, trainable GeM and scalar head. First-stage budgets are positive five-epoch multiples; all eight fits precede the teacher mean. Stage two continues each own checkpoint for ten epochs with fresh constant-rate Adam and SmoothL1. Preserve source target refinement, augmentation and partial batches. Exact checkpoint prediction replay and cleanup on success or failure. RNG state changes. No historical training or accuracy parity claim.

parameters.seeds: Exactly eight family/replica tuple keys with distinct nonnegative 32-bit integer seeds.

parameters.upper_deviation: Explicit finite nonnegative upper refinement deviation, checked by second_stage_targets.

parameters.work_root: Existing private parent directory; the implementation removes its temporary checkpoint subdirectory.

providers.signature: (values: numpy.ndarray, cut_points: numpy.ndarray, tie_policy: str) -> numpy.ndarray

seed_fields.description: Return the index of each value among strictly increasing cut points. Inputs are finite one-dimensional float32 or float64 arrays. Values must be nonempty; an empty cut vector assigns index zero to every value. 'upper' places equality above a cut; 'lower' places equality below it. Use NumPy searchsorted without rounding, clipping or casting either input. Return a fresh integer vector with indices from zero through the number of cuts. Inputs remain unchanged. Boundaries, units, class names and interpretation are caller policy; no calibration or learning occurs.

providers.operation: Assign each numeric value an index among ordered cut points.
providers.plain_limits: Use finite vectors and strictly increasing cuts. Choose which side receives equality. Empty cuts are allowed. Inputs stay unchanged.
providers.validity_bounds: One-dimensional native float32 or float64 NumPy arrays, both finite; values nonempty, cuts optionally empty and strictly increasing. Use numpy.searchsorted without rounding, clipping or casting. Upper means side=right; lower means side=left. Return a fresh integer vector from zero through the number of cuts. Mixed float32/float64 inputs follow NumPy comparison semantics. No labels, probability bounds, fixed thresholds or calibration are imposed.

parameters.values: Nonempty finite one-dimensional float32 or float64 ndarray.
parameters.cut_points: Finite one-dimensional float32 or float64 ndarray of strictly increasing cut points; may be empty.
parameters.tie_policy: Explicit upper or lower string controlling exact equality at a cut.

providers.outputs: Fresh integer ndarray aligned with values, with indices in [0, number of cuts].
providers.reuse: Domain independent ordered interval indexing for any compatible numeric quantities. Units, thresholds, category names and downstream interpretation belong to the caller.

intake_stage_mapping.image_standardization: Plain full-image resizing replaces unsupported retinal cropping/local-color subtraction. Reference augmentation and publisher normalization are explicit choices.
intake_stage_mapping.cnn_backbone: Eight models: two each of Inception-ResNet-v2, Inception-v4, SE-ResNeXt-50 and SE-ResNeXt-101, with trainable GeM and scalar regression head. EfficientNet substitution excluded.
intake_stage_mapping.quadratic_weighted_kappa_qwk_loss: Smooth-L1 regression replaces unsupported differentiable-QWK training loss. QWK motivates final fixed ordinal thresholds, not the training objective.
intake_stage_mapping.pre_training_fine_tuning: All pretrained backbone parameters train in stage one; an ensemble teacher builds three added target roles, and each own model continues ten epochs. Four-level grouping differs from five-level averaging labels.
intake_stage_mapping.threshold_calibration: Fixed manually selected cuts 0.7,1.5,2.5,3.5 replace unsupported Nelder-Mead optimization. Equality convention is explicit.

limitations: Automated Community Tier 3 reference; no human-reviewed Tier 1 or usage-qualified Tier 2 designation.
Corrected eight-model CPU reconstruction; original winner runtime, artifact identity and leaderboard equivalence remain unproven.
First-stage budgets in five-epoch increments, Adam settings, ensemble teacher and fresh second-stage optimizer are explicit reference choices.
Augmentation units/distributions/order, bilinear resize, publisher normalization, scalar head and single-view inference are explicit choices.
Symmetric group bounds and threshold equality convention are explicit; the source establishes only the demonstrated lower-bound example.
Caller establishes population-role provenance and physical-image identity; supplied-label queries reject, while pseudo-label queries are deliberately transductive.
Synthetic full-resolution execution uses five first-stage and ten second-stage epochs per model; original population-scale performance is unproven.
Local external model artifacts require caller use rights. Each call retrains; temporary checkpoints are verified and removed.
Retain pooling, upstream, dependency and supplemental notices with the reconstruction.
Caller supplies model artifacts they are entitled to use; integrity and source correspondence checks do not establish usage rights.
Smp-hub cards declare license other; no independent model-weight grant or redistribution permission is inferred.
Review future distribution of external model artifacts or dependency wheels separately.
Pinned maintainer mirror identity is established; exact winner artifact/runtime identity and competitive accuracy remain unproven.
The training body is AST-equivalent to the qualified reference apart from returning the equality policy and moving final cut indexing into the graph.
Full graph validation checks complete fits, optimizer updates, checkpoint replay, target roles and the ensemble/cut oracle; it does not compare all trained tensors across independent runs.
Cut indexing is domain independent; fixed source cuts, image models, target roles and learner settings remain recipe policy.
Intermediate result dictionaries must come from the same invocation; the result encoder alone cannot establish training provenance.
Provider publication, corrected original intake and served selection remain separate requirements.
Automated Tier 3 only; no Tier 1 human certification or Tier 2 usage qualification.
Generic cut indexing is domain independent. The recipe supplies its fixed cuts and caller equality policy through explicit graph edges.
Synthetic training qualification does not establish competition accuracy, historical trained-weight parity or independent-run tensor identity.
Installed package hashes were checked against their own RECORD files, not independently authenticated publisher signatures. Clean deployment qualification is not claimed.
Validation bounds native and Torch thread pools to one; deployment must configure its own resource limits.
External pretrained artifacts are runtime dependencies; their access does not establish redistribution rights.
Software dependencies are separate from registered atom dependencies. This review alone does not approve catalog records.
